title: Giotto’s Campanile
visualBrief: Florentine polychrome marble campanile, with reinforced octagonal corners, hexagonal and diamond relief cycles, statue niches, paired biforas and a three-light belfry loggia, Gothic gables, projecting corbels and an open flat crown.

nativeAxes.front: −Z is the cathedral-facing north entrance elevation
nativeAxes.origin: Exact-QID mapped shaft center at exterior pavement

scaleBasis: Opera del Duomo published 84.7 m height and roughly 15 m square base; mapped reinforced-corner plan determines shaft width and alignment. Photographer Roberto Di Ferdinando’s exterior image and Opera descriptions establish loggia/window and marble-panel hierarchy.

geographicProposal.evidence: Exact-QID reinforced-corner outline supplies the nearly north/south facade axis. The museum’s cathedral-side rear entrance determines the authored −Z face; the square plan otherwise permits quarter turns.
geographicProposal.limitations: Top crown projects beyond the mapped shaft, as visible in the reference. Exterior paving and temporary restoration scaffolding are excluded.
geographicProposal.notes: Exact-QID reinforced-corner outline supplies the nearly north/south facade axis. geometrySource: Original deterministic geometry informed by cited dimensions, measured plans and photographs. No downloaded mesh or photographic texture is embedded.
sourceLicense: Original geometry under repository license. Map-derived outline information is attributed to OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications retain their own rights.
materialMethod: Shared material graphs with metric repeat UV0 and original vertex tints; GLB PBR fallback remains self-contained. No per-model texture duplication.
limitations: The narrative bas-reliefs and statues retain their counts, shapes and architectural niches but are original simplified sculptural reliefs, not reproductions of the individual named artworks.
Panel elevations, marble flower designs, moulding sections and window tracery are fitted to exterior photography. Exact conservation stone-cut patterns are not claimed.
Permanent exterior is modeled; temporary restoration scaffolding is excluded.

Current browser levels deliberately aggregate distant inlays/sculpture/rails and omit subpixel robe folds and tiny fittings. Geometric figures and reliefs preserve the architectural program rather than individual artworks. No surveyed pavement grade or physical-device performance claim.
reviewStatus: medium-fi; current hash-bound visual acceptance recorded in qa.json

appearance.identity: Polychrome white/green/rose marble, octagonal reinforced corners,26 hexagonal and28 diamond lower relief panels,16 statue niches, paired biforas and three-light belfry, Gothic gables and an open flat roof terrace.
appearance.master: Keep the current detailed source and imported master byte-identical. Browser levels use explicit component sampling rather than a whole-mesh reduction.
appearance.browser: Skyline retains the full height/footprint, north recess, three loggia levels and open terrace. District adds grouped rose/green corner inlays, both narrative panel cycles,16 niche figures and coarse Gothic surrounds. Street restores more corner fields, three-dimensional figures, mullions, tracery, pinnacles and open crown posts. Closeup restores15 corner fields, four arch-band rings, geometric rosettes, profiled columns and sparse crockets. Fine marble inlays use flat colored surfaces on the shared neutral marble graph.
appearance.scope: Full static architectural exterior with the existing original geometric artwork reconstructions; not literal casts or inscriptions. Retained exact-QID center, facade axes and cathedral-facing north entrance. Ground contact remains host-supplied nominal pavement.
